claims.text: The target materials are as-cast, single-phase, microstructurally homogeneous high-entropy alloys intended for thermal-insulation applications.
The proposed model combines descriptors of local lattice distortion, disorder, and phonon dispersion.
Including multidimensional lattice-disorder and phonon-dispersion descriptors will improve prediction of phonon thermal conductivity relative to compositional averaging.
Local lattice disorder produces phonon-scattering centers in high-entropy alloys.
These phonon-scattering centers directly modulate phonon mean free paths.
Subtle variations in local lattice distortion affect phonon-scattering events.
More accurate representation of phonon-scattering events enables more accurate estimation of phonon mean free paths.
More accurate phonon mean-free-path estimates lead to more accurate predictions of phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed model will outperform empirical, interpolation-based, or linear compositional-averaging methods.
The proposed model will identify alloys with lower phonon thermal conductivity and therefore improved insulation performance.
Improved prediction will be manifested as closer agreement between predicted and measured phonon thermal conductivities.
The relevant baseline methods estimate thermal conductivity using compositional interpolation or linear averaging of constituent properties.
The model is applicable only to single-phase high-entropy alloys in which phonons carry most of the heat.
The model may not apply to phase-separated systems, alloys with strong electronic heat conduction, or systems where disorder is not the dominant scattering mechanism.
TDTR or laser-flash analysis can be used in the benchmark to determine phonon thermal conductivity.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on the alloy system and the quality of the model's input descriptors.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant accuracy improvement over traditional methods would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of model-selected alloys to have lower thermal conductivity than conventionally selected controls would falsify the hypothesis.
